rot.ideia.ex1.e1: Now the rook has two bishops to help. With so much force, your king does not even need to come close.
rot.ideia.ex1.e2: Count the black king's squares: the bishop on h6 attacks g7, and the bishop on d3 attacks h7.
rot.ideia.ex1.e3: Only the last rank is left to close, with a rook check.
rot.ideia.ex1.certo: Checkmate! The rook closes the last rank, and the bishops guard g7 and h7.
rot.ideia.ex1.revela: The rook goes to a8 and checks along the edge. Every escape square is taken.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.h6g5.1: The bishop left the g7 diagonal, and there was no check.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.h6g5.2: The black king runs to g7.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.h6g5.3: Let's go back: the bishops stay, and the rook gives the check.
rot.ideia.ex1.fora: That move does not give mate. Let's go back to the position.
rot.ideia.ex1.l1: Remember: each bishop takes one square, and the rook closes the edge.
rot.ideia.ex2.e1: The rook on the seventh traps the black king on the last rank. It walks between f8, g8 and h8.
rot.ideia.ex2.e2: One bishop already guards h7. Take the other one to the diagonal through f8; then the king will only have h8.
rot.ideia.ex2.p: Prepare the mate with a bishop, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.certo: That's right! From h6, the bishop takes f8 and g7. The black king only has h8.
rot.ideia.ex2.revela: The bishop goes to h6 and takes f8. The black king is left with only h8.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.a7a8.1: It is check, but the rook left the seventh and freed the king.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.a7a8.2: The black king escapes to g7.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.a7a8.3: Let's go back: first the bishop, then the rook.
rot.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not prepare the mate. Let's go back to the position.
rot.ideia.ex2.volta: Prepare the mate with a bishop, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.l1: The black king goes to h8, its only square.
rot.ideia.ex2.l2: Checkmate! The h6 bishop guards g7, and the d3 bishop guards h7.
rot.ideia.ex2.l3: Now I will show the net built step by step, and a danger: stalemate.
rot.demos.rede.e1: Watch the rook and the two bishops take all the black king's squares, without help from the white king.
rot.demos.rede.l1: The rook goes to the seventh and traps the king on the last rank.
rot.demos.rede.l2: The black king goes to f8.
rot.demos.rede.l3: The king could go to e8. The bishop goes to g6 and takes that square.
rot.demos.rede.l4: Count: e8 and the seventh are taken. The king goes back to g8.
rot.demos.rede.l5: The other bishop goes to h6 and takes f8.
rot.demos.rede.l7: Checkmate! The bishops guard g7 and h7, and the rook closes the edge.
rot.demos.afogamento.e1: Now a danger. The rook and the h6 bishop guard g7 and h7. Only g8 is left.
rot.demos.afogamento.l1: If the d3 bishop went to c4, it would take g8 without check. The king would have no move: stalemate.
rot.demos.afogamento.l2: The rook solves it: it gives check and takes g8 at the same time. Checkmate!
rot.demos.afogamento.l3: Now it's your turn: trap the king with the rook, take squares with the bishops and count the escapes.
rot.pratica.preparar.enunciado: Give checkmate. The black king has a8 and c8. Attack c8 with a bishop that also guards b7.
rot.pratica.preparar.fim: Perfect. The bishop took c8, and the rook gave mate.
rot.pratica.preparar.err.h7h8: It is check, but the rook left the seventh, and the king escapes. Try again.
rot.pratica.preparar.err.f1h3: The bishop takes c8, but does not guard b7. Find the square that guards both.
rot.pratica.centro.enunciado: The black king is in the center. Trap it on a rank with the rook and use the bishops to take squares.
rot.pratica.centro.fim: Well done. You knew how to use the two bishops.
